paragraphs.text: וַיַּאַסְפ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיֵּאָ֣סְפ֔וּ שֹׂכֹ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִיהוּדָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בֵּין־שׂוֹכֹ֥ה וּבֵין־עֲזֵקָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥פֶס דַּמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: Now the Pelishtim gathered their armies for battle, and they were gathered at Sokhoh, which belongs to Yehudah, and encamped between Sokhoh and Azeqah, in Efes-Dammim.

notes.official: Pelishtim = Philistines (central `pelishtim-caphtor`); Sokhoh = Socoh; Yehudah = Judah; Azeqah = Azekah; Efes-Dammim = Ephes-dammim (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *maḥănêhem* 'their armies', literally 'their camps'.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁא֤וּל וְאִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נֶאֶסְפ֔וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעֵ֣מֶק הָאֵלָ֑ה וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And Sha'ul and the men of Yisra'el were gathered and encamped in the valley of Elah, and drew up the battle in array to meet the Pelishtim.

notes.official: Sha'ul = Saul; *bəʿēmeq hāʾēlâ* 'in the valley of Elah', 'valley of the terebinth', kept as a name (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *wayyaʿarḵû milḥāmâ* 'and drew up the battle in array'.

paragraphs.text: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֞ים עֹמְדִ֤ים אֶל־הָהָר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֹמְדִ֥ים אֶל־הָהָ֖ר מִזֶּ֑ה וְהַגַּ֖יְא בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And the Pelishtim stood on the mountain on the one side, and Yisra'el stood on the mountain on the other side; and the valley was between them.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֤א אִֽישׁ־הַבֵּנַ֙יִם֙ מִמַּחֲנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים גָּלְיָ֥ת שְׁמ֖וֹ מִגַּ֑ת גָּבְה֕וֹ שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת וָזָֽרֶת׃

i18n.en: And there went out a champion from the camps of the Pelishtim, named Golyat, of Gat, whose height was six cubits and a span.

notes.official: *ʾîš-habbēnayim* 'a champion' (ASV): literally 'the man of the space between', the warrior who fights between the lines in single combat (also v 23; cf. 2 Sam 2:14-16). Golyat = Goliath; Gat = Gath (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *gāḇhô šēš ʾammôṯ wāzāreṯ* 'whose height was six cubits and a span' (about 2.9 m): the MT figure is kept. The LXX (Codex Vaticanus and the Lucianic text), 4QSamᵃ and Josephus (*Ant.* 6.171) read 'four cubits and a span' (about 2 m), which many consider the earlier reading (McCarter, *I Samuel*) (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְכ֤וֹבַע נְחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְשִׁרְי֥וֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂ֖ים ה֣וּא לָב֑וּשׁ וּמִשְׁקַל֙ הַשִּׁרְי֔וֹן חֲמֵשֶׁת־אֲלָפִ֥ים שְׁקָלִ֖ים נְחֹֽשֶֽׁת׃

i18n.en: And he had a helmet of bronze on his head, and he was clothed with a coat of scale mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of bronze.

notes.official: *kôḇaʿ nəḥōšeṯ* 'a helmet of bronze'. *širyôn qaśqaśśîm* 'a coat of scale mail': *qaśqeśeṯ* is the scale of a fish (Lev 11:9), so this is scale armour; the ASV 'coat of mail' leaves out the scales. Plain *širyôn* at v 38. *ḥămēšeṯ-ʾălāp̄îm šəqālîm* 'five thousand shekels', about 57 kg.

paragraphs.text: וּמִצְחַ֥ת נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־רַגְלָ֑יו וְכִיד֥וֹן נְחֹ֖שֶׁת בֵּ֥ין כְּתֵפָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he had greaves of bronze on his legs, and a javelin of bronze between his shoulders.

notes.official: *miṣḥaṯ nəḥōšeṯ* 'greaves of bronze'. *kîḏôn* 'javelin' (ASV): in the War Scroll (1QM) *kîḏôn* is a sword, and some render 'scimitar' here, but the ASV is kept.

paragraphs.text: וחץ [וְעֵ֣ץ] חֲנִית֗וֹ כִּמְנוֹר֙ אֹֽרְגִ֔ים וְלַהֶ֣בֶת חֲנִית֔וֹ שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת שְׁקָלִ֖ים בַּרְזֶ֑ל וְנֹשֵׂ֥א הַצִּנָּ֖ה הֹלֵ֥ךְ לְפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the head of his spear weighed six hundred shekels of iron; and the shield-bearer went before him.

notes.official: *wəʿēṣ ḥănîṯô* 'And the shaft of his spear' translates the Qere *wəʿēṣ* 'and the wood of'; the Ketiv *wḥṣ* 'and the arrow of' is a graphic variant (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`). *kimnôr ʾōrəḡîm* 'like a weaver's beam', perhaps a spear fitted with a loop and cord like the leash rod of a loom (Yadin, 'Goliath's Javelin and the *mənôr ʾōrəḡîm*', PEQ 87, 1955). *wəlahebeṯ ḥănîṯô* 'the head of his spear', 600 shekels, about 7 kg.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד וַיִּקְרָא֙ אֶל־מַעַרְכֹ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לָ֥מָּה תֵצְא֖וּ לַעֲרֹ֣ךְ מִלְחָמָ֑ה הֲל֧וֹא אָנֹכִ֣י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗י וְאַתֶּם֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְשָׁא֔וּל בְּרוּ־לָכֶ֥ם אִ֖ישׁ וְיֵרֵ֥ד אֵלָֽי׃

i18n.en: And he stood and cried out to the armies of Yisra'el, and said to them, "Why have you come out to draw up the battle in array? Am I not the Pelishtite, and you servants of Sha'ul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

notes.official: *hălôʾ ʾānōḵî happəlištî* 'Am I not the Pelishtite': the singular gentilic *happəlištî* is 'the Pelishtite' under the '-ite' rule, and the plural *pəlištîm* is 'the Pelishtim' as fixed by central `pelishtim-caphtor` (ASV 'the Philistine', 'the Philistines') (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *maʿarḵôṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'the armies of Yisra'el' (ASV), literally 'the battle lines' (also vv 10, 26, 36, 45).

paragraphs.text: אִם־יוּכַ֞ל לְהִלָּחֵ֤ם אִתִּי֙ וְהִכָּ֔נִי וְהָיִ֥ינוּ לָכֶ֖ם לַעֲבָדִ֑ים וְאִם־אֲנִ֤י אֽוּכַל־לוֹ֙ וְהִכִּיתִ֔יו וִהְיִ֤יתֶם לָ֙נוּ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֖ם אֹתָֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: If he is able to fight with me and kill me, then we will be your servants; but if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and serve us."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אֲנִ֗י חֵרַ֛פְתִּי אֶת־מַעַרְכ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה תְּנוּ־לִ֣י אִ֔ישׁ וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֖ה יָֽחַד׃

i18n.en: And the Pelishtite said, "I defy the armies of Yisra'el this day; give me a man, that we may fight together."

notes.official: *ʾănî ḥēraptî ʾeṯ-maʿarḵôṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'I defy the armies of Yisra'el': *ḥrp* 'taunt, reproach' is the key verb of the chapter (vv 10, 25, 26, 36, 45).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע שָׁאוּל֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּחַ֥תּוּ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And when Sha'ul and all Yisra'el heard these words of the Pelishtite, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.

paragraphs.text: וְדָוִד֩ בֶּן־אִ֨ישׁ אֶפְרָתִ֜י הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֙חֶם֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה וּשְׁמ֣וֹ יִשַׁ֔י וְל֖וֹ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וְהָאִישׁ֙ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל זָקֵ֖ן בָּ֥א בַאֲנָשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: Now David was the son of that Efratite of Beit-Lechem in Yehudah, whose name was Yishai; and he had eight sons; and the man was old in the days of Sha'ul, advanced among men.

notes.official: *ben-ʾîš ʾep̄rāṯî hazzeh* 'the son of that Efratite' (Ephrathite), of Efrat, the clan around Beit-Lechem (Bethlehem); Yishai = Jesse (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *bāʾ ḇaʾănāšîm* 'advanced among men' (MT; ASV 'stricken [in years] among men'); the Lucianic Greek and the Syriac read 'advanced in years' (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). Verses 12-31 are absent from the LXX of Codex Vaticanus, which also lacks vv 41, 48b, 50 and 55-58 (and 18:1-5) and so preserves a shorter form of the story. Whether the shorter text is earlier is debated (Barthélemy, Gooding, Lust and Tov, *The Story of David and Goliath*, OBO 73, 1986). The full MT is translated without marking (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת בְּנֵֽי־יִשַׁי֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֔ים הָלְכ֥וּ אַחֲרֵי־שָׁא֖וּל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֣ם ׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלְכוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֱלִיאָ֣ב הַבְּכ֗וֹר וּמִשְׁנֵ֙הוּ֙ אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖י שַׁמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And the three eldest sons of Yishai had gone after Sha'ul to the battle; and the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eli'av the firstborn, and next to him Avinadav, and the third Shammah.

notes.official: Eli'av = Eliab; Avinadav = Abinadab; Shammah (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְדָוִ֖ד ה֣וּא הַקָּטָ֑ן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֔ים הָלְכ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And David was the youngest; and the three eldest followed Sha'ul.

paragraphs.text: וְדָוִ֛ד הֹלֵ֥ךְ וָשָׁ֖ב מֵעַ֣ל שָׁא֑וּל לִרְע֛וֹת אֶת־צֹ֥אן אָבִ֖יו בֵּֽית־לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: Now David went back and forth from Sha'ul to tend his father's sheep at Beit-Lechem.

notes.official: *hōlēḵ wāšāḇ mēʿal šāʾûl* 'went back and forth from Sha'ul', which reconciles David's service at court (16:21-23) with his presence at home.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגַּ֥שׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְהַעֲרֵ֑ב וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֖ב אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the Pelishtite drew near morning and evening, and took his stand forty days.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשַׁ֜י לְדָוִ֣ד בְּנ֗וֹ קַח־נָ֤א לְאַחֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵיפַ֤ת הַקָּלִיא֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וַעֲשָׂרָ֥ה לֶ֖חֶם הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָרֵ֥ץ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה לְאַחֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And Yishai said to David his son, "Take now for your brothers an ephah of this parched grain and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to your brothers;

notes.official: *ʾêp̄aṯ haqqālîʾ hazzeh* 'an ephah of this parched grain'.

paragraphs.text: וְ֠אֵת עֲשֶׂ֜רֶת חֲרִצֵ֤י הֶֽחָלָב֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה תָּבִ֖יא לְשַׂר־הָאָ֑לֶף וְאֶת־אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּפְקֹ֣ד לְשָׁל֔וֹם וְאֶת־עֲרֻבָּתָ֖ם תִּקָּֽח׃

i18n.en: and bring these ten cheeses to the captain of the thousand, and see how your brothers fare, and take their pledge."

notes.official: *ʿăśereṯ ḥăriṣê heḥālāḇ* 'ten cheeses' (literally 'cuts of milk'); *śar-hāʾelep̄* 'the captain of the thousand'; *ʿărubbāṯām tiqqāḥ* 'take their pledge', a token that they are well.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁא֤וּל וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּעֵ֖מֶק הָֽאֵלָ֑ה נִלְחָמִ֖ים עִם־פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

i18n.en: Now Sha'ul and they and all the men of Yisra'el were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Pelishtim.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם דָּוִ֜ד בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּטֹּ֤שׁ אֶת־הַצֹּאן֙ עַל־שֹׁמֵ֔ר וַיִּשָּׂ֣א וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יִשָׁ֑י וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּעְגָּ֔לָה וְהַחַ֗יִל הַיֹּצֵא֙ אֶל־הַמַּ֣עֲרָכָ֔ה וְהֵרֵ֖עוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And David rose early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took up his load and went, as Yishai had commanded him; and he came to the place of the wagons as the army that was going out to the battle line was shouting the war cry.

notes.official: *hammaʿgālâ* 'the place of the wagons' (ASV), perhaps the ring of wagons or the barricade around the camp (NRSV 'the encampment'). *wəhēreʿû bammilḥāmâ* 'shouting the war cry' (*rwʿ*, cf. Josh 6:5).

paragraphs.text: וַתַּעֲרֹ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מַעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את מַעֲרָכָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el and the Pelishtim drew up in battle array, army against army.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּטֹּשׁ֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־הַכֵּלִ֜ים מֵעָלָ֗יו עַל־יַד֙ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַכֵּלִ֔ים וַיָּ֖רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לְאֶחָ֖יו לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the army, and came and greeted his brothers.

notes.official: *hakkēlîm* 'his baggage'; *wayyišʾal ləʾeḥāyw ləšālôm* 'and greeted his brothers'.

paragraphs.text: וְה֣וּא ׀ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֣ישׁ הַבֵּנַ֡יִם עוֹלֶ֞ה גָּלְיָת֩ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י שְׁמ֤וֹ מִגַּת֙ ממערות [מִמַּעַרְכ֣וֹת] פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִֽד׃

i18n.en: And as he talked with them, behold, the champion, the Pelishtite of Gat, Golyat by name, came up out of the ranks of the Pelishtim, and spoke according to the same words; and David heard them.

notes.official: *mimmaʿarḵôṯ pəlištîm* 'out of the ranks of the Pelishtim' translates the Qere (ASV 'out of the ranks'); the Ketiv *mmʿrwt* 'from the caves' is a graphic variant (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`). 'the champion' (see v 4); 'the Pelishtite of Gat' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְכֹל֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּרְאוֹתָ֖ם אֶת־הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּנֻ֙סוּ֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And all the men of Yisra'el, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ הָאִ֤ישׁ הָֽעֹלֶה֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י לְחָרֵ֥ף אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹלֶ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה הָאִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יַכֶּ֜נּוּ יַעְשְׁרֶ֥נּוּ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ׀ עֹ֣שֶׁר גָּד֗וֹל וְאֶת־בִּתּוֹ֙ יִתֶּן־ל֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה חָפְשִׁ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And the men of Yisra'el said, "Have you seen this man who has come up? Surely to defy Yisra'el he has come up. And it shall be that the man who kills him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Yisra'el."

notes.official: *wəʾeṯ-bêṯ ʾāḇîw yaʿăśeh ḥop̄šî* 'and make his father's house free', exempt from taxes or service.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶֽל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים הָעֹמְדִ֣ים עִמּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ מַה־יֵּעָשֶׂ֗ה לָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַכֶּה֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַלָּ֔ז וְהֵסִ֥יר חֶרְפָּ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י מִ֗י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֤י הֶֽעָרֵל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכ֖וֹת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And David spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, "What shall be done for the man who kills this Pelishtite and takes away the reproach from Yisra'el? For who is this uncircumcised Pelishtite, that he should defy the armies of the living Elohim?"

notes.official:
*maʿarḵôṯ ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm* 'the armies of the living Elohim' (ASV 'the armies of the living God'): *ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm* is anarthrous, and the adjective *ḥayyîm* is plural, agreeing with the form of *ʾĕlōhîm* (also v 36; Deut 5:23 [ET 5:26]; Jer 10:10; 23:36), where *ʾēl ḥay* has the singular (Josh 3:10; Hos 2:1). English needs a determiner before an attributive adjective, so the article is supplied (clause 7 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). The epithet sets YHWH, who acts, against gods who do not (cf. Jer 10:10-11). *hāʿārēl* 'uncircumcised' (`brit-milah-circumcision-covenant`), Israel's epithet for the Pelishtim. *wəhēsîr ḥerpâ* 'and takes away the reproach'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('the armies of the living God') and reads 'living' as showing that a tangible divine presence was among the people at that time. The line renders *ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm* literally and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יֵעָשֶׂ֔ה לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַכֶּֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, "So shall it be done for the man who kills him."

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֱלִיאָב֙ אָחִ֣יו הַגָּד֔וֹל בְּדַבְּר֖וֹ אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיִּֽחַר־אַף֩ אֱלִיאָ֨ב בְּדָוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ לָמָּה־זֶּ֣ה יָרַ֗דְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֨י נָטַ֜שְׁתָּ מְעַ֨ט הַצֹּ֤אן הָהֵ֙נָּה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אֲנִ֧י יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶת־זְדֹנְךָ֗ וְאֵת֙ רֹ֣עַ לְבָבֶ֔ךָ כִּ֗י לְמַ֛עַן רְא֥וֹת הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה יָרָֽדְתָּ׃

i18n.en: And Eli'av his eldest brother heard when he spoke to the men; and Eli'av's anger burned against David, and he said, "Why have you come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart; for you have come down to see the battle."

notes.official: *ʾănî yāḏaʿtî ʾeṯ-zəḏōnəḵā* 'I know your presumption' (ASV 'pride').

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתִי עָ֑תָּה הֲל֖וֹא דָּבָ֥ר הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: And David said, "What have I done now? Is there not a cause?"

notes.official: *hălôʾ dāḇār hûʾ* 'Is there not a cause?' (ASV): *dāḇār* is 'word, matter', and the phrase may also mean 'It was only a word!' (cf. NJPS 'I was only asking!'). The ASV is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסֹּ֤ב מֵֽאֶצְלוֹ֙ אֶל־מ֣וּל אַחֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְשִׁבֻ֤הוּ הָעָם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּדָּבָ֖ר הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

i18n.en: And he turned away from him toward another, and spoke after the same manner; and the people answered him again as before.

paragraphs.text: וַיְּשָּֽׁמְעוּ֙ הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לִפְנֵֽי־שָׁא֖וּל וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And when the words which David spoke were heard, they reported them before Sha'ul; and he sent for him.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל אַל־יִפֹּ֥ל לֵב־אָדָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו עַבְדְּךָ֣ יֵלֵ֔ךְ וְנִלְחַ֖ם עִם־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֥י הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And David said to Sha'ul, "Let no man's heart fail because of him; your servant will go and fight with this Pelishtite."

notes.official: *ʾal-yippōl lēḇ-ʾāḏām ʿālāyw* 'Let no man's heart fail because of him' (MT). The LXX reads 'my lord's heart' (= *lēḇ-ʾăḏōnî*), which many adopt (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד לֹ֤א תוּכַל֙ לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַזֶּ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־נַ֣עַר אַ֔תָּה וְה֛וּא אִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֖ה מִנְּעֻרָֽיו׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Sha'ul said to David, "You are not able to go against this Pelishtite to fight with him; for you are a youth, and he has been a man of war from his youth."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל רֹעֶ֨ה הָיָ֧ה עַבְדְּךָ֛ לְאָבִ֖יו בַּצֹּ֑אן וּבָ֤א הָֽאֲרִי֙ וְאֶת־הַדּ֔וֹב וְנָשָׂ֥א שֶׂ֖ה מֵהָעֵֽדֶר׃

i18n.en: And David said to Sha'ul, "Your servant was keeping sheep for his father; and when a lion came, or a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock,

notes.official: *hāʾărî wəʾeṯ-haddôḇ* 'a lion, or a bear': the *wəʾeṯ* before the second animal is unusual and is rendered by the sense.

paragraphs.text: וְיָצָ֧אתִי אַחֲרָ֛יו וְהִכִּתִ֖יו וְהִצַּ֣לְתִּי מִפִּ֑יו וַיָּ֣קָם עָלַ֔י וְהֶחֱזַ֙קְתִּי֙ בִּזְקָנ֔וֹ וְהִכִּתִ֖יו וַהֲמִיתִּֽיו׃

i18n.en: I went out after it and struck it and delivered it out of its mouth; and when it rose against me, I caught it by its beard and struck it and killed it.

notes.official: *wəheḥĕzaqtî bizqānô* 'I caught it by its beard', that is, by the jaw.

paragraphs.text: גַּ֧ם אֶֽת־הָאֲרִ֛י גַּם־הַדּ֖וֹב הִכָּ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֽ֠הָיָה הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י הֶעָרֵ֤ל הַזֶּה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכֹ֖ת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Your servant has struck both the lion and the bear; and this uncircumcised Pelishtite shall be as one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living Elohim."

notes.official: *maʿarḵōṯ ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm* 'the armies of the living Elohim', as v 26 (clause 7 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`); *hāʿārēl* 'uncircumcised' (`brit-milah-circumcision-covenant`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ דָּוִד֒ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּלַ֜נִי מִיַּ֤ד הָֽאֲרִי֙ וּמִיַּ֣ד הַדֹּ֔ב ה֣וּא יַצִּילֵ֔נִי מִיַּ֥ד הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הַזֶּ֑ה (ס) וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֤וּל אֶל־דָּוִד֙ לֵ֔ךְ וַֽיהוָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And David said, "YHWH who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this Pelishtite." And Sha'ul said to David, "Go, and YHWH shall be with you."

notes.official: The MT has a section mark within the verse after 'this Pelishtite' (`piska-b-emtza-pasuq-masoretic-paragraph-break`). *lēḵ waYHWH yihyeh ʿimmāḵ* 'Go, and YHWH shall be with you' (`elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּלְבֵּ֨שׁ שָׁא֤וּל אֶת־דָּוִד֙ מַדָּ֔יו וְנָתַ֛ן ק֥וֹבַע נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיַּלְבֵּ֥שׁ אֹת֖וֹ שִׁרְיֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And Sha'ul clothed David with his garments, and he put a helmet of bronze on his head, and he clothed him with a coat of mail.

notes.official: *maddāw* 'his garments', the military tunic; *qôḇaʿ nəḥōšeṯ* 'a helmet of bronze'; *širyôn* 'a coat of mail' (cf. v 5).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּחְגֹּ֣ר דָּוִ֣ד אֶת־חַ֠רְבּוֹ מֵעַ֨ל לְמַדָּ֜יו וַיֹּ֣אֶל לָלֶכֶת֮ כִּ֣י לֹֽא־נִסָּה֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־שָׁא֗וּל לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָלֶ֥כֶת בָּאֵ֖לֶּה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נִסִּ֑יתִי וַיְסִרֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖ד מֵעָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And David girded his sword over his garments, and he tried to go, for he had not tested them. And David said to Sha'ul, "I cannot go with these, for I have not tested them." And David took them off.

notes.official: *kî lōʾ-nissâ* 'for he had not tested them': David is unpractised in armour.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מַקְל֜וֹ בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּבְחַר־ל֣וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה חַלֻּקֵֽי־אֲבָנִ֣ים ׀ מִן־הַנַּ֡חַל וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹ֠תָם בִּכְלִ֨י הָרֹעִ֧ים אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ וּבַיַּלְק֖וּט וְקַלְּע֣וֹ בְיָד֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֖שׁ אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the shepherd's bag which he had, in his pouch; and his sling was in his hand; and he drew near to the Pelishtite.

notes.official: *ḥămiššâ ḥallūqê-ʾăḇānîm* 'five smooth stones'; *bikəlî hārōʿîm ʾăšer-lô ûḇayyalqûṭ* 'in the shepherd's bag which he had, in his pouch' (*yalqûṭ* occurs only here); *wəqalʿô* 'and his sling'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְקָרֵ֖ב אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וְהָאִ֛ישׁ נֹשֵׂ֥א הַצִּנָּ֖ה לְפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And the Pelishtite came on and drew near to David, and the man who carried the shield went before him.

notes.official: Absent from LXX Vaticanus (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`; see v 12).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּבֵּ֧ט הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛י וַיִּרְאֶ֥ה אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד וַיִּבְזֵ֑הוּ כִּֽי־הָיָ֣ה נַ֔עַר וְאַדְמֹנִ֖י עִם־יְפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And when the Pelishtite looked and saw David, he despised him; for he was a youth, and ruddy, and beautiful of appearance.

notes.official: *wayyiḇzēhû* 'he despised him'. *ʾaḏmōnî ʿim-yəp̄ēh marʾeh* 'ruddy, and beautiful of appearance' (`eshet-yefat-mareh`; cf. 16:12).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד הֲכֶ֣לֶב אָנֹ֔כִי כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה בָֽא־אֵלַ֖י בַּמַּקְל֑וֹת וַיְקַלֵּ֧ל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛י אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד בֵּאלֹהָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And the Pelishtite said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?" And the Pelishtite cursed David by his elohim.

notes.official: *hăḵeleḇ ʾānōḵî* 'Am I a dog'; *bammaqlôṯ* 'with sticks' (David carries one staff, v 40). *wayqallēl happəlištî ʾeṯ-dāwiḏ bēʾlōhāyw* 'And the Pelishtite cursed David by his elohim': lower case for the Pelishti gods (clause 4 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד לְכָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י וְאֶתְּנָה֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂ֣רְךָ֔ לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the Pelishtite said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the skies and to the beasts of the field."

notes.official: *ləʿôp̄ haššāmayim* 'to the birds of the skies' (central `shamayim`); *ûləḇehĕmaṯ haśśāḏeh* 'and to the beasts of the field'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אַתָּה֙ בָּ֣א אֵלַ֔י בְּחֶ֖רֶב וּבַחֲנִ֣ית וּבְכִיד֑וֹן וְאָנֹכִ֣י בָֽא־אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּשֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֛י מַעַרְכ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר חֵרַֽפְתָּ׃

i18n.en: Then David said to the Pelishtite, "You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of YHWH of hosts, the Elohim of the armies of Yisra'el, whom you have defied.

notes.official: *bəšēm YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ* 'in the name of YHWH of hosts' (`yhwh-tsevaot-yhwh-of-hosts-former-prophets`) *ʾĕlōhê maʿarḵôṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'the Elohim of the armies of Yisra'el' (clause 3 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`): the apposition connects the title with Israel's battle lines. *kîḏôn* 'javelin' (see v 6).

paragraphs.text: הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֡ה יְסַגֶּרְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה בְּיָדִ֜י וְהִכִּיתִ֗ךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִ֤י אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵעָלֶ֔יךָ וְנָ֨תַתִּ֜י פֶּ֣גֶר מַחֲנֵ֤ה פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְחַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: This day YHWH will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you and take your head from off you; and I will give the corpses of the camp of the Pelishtim this day to the birds of the skies and to the wild beasts of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is Elohim in Yisra'el;

notes.official: *yəsaggerḵā YHWH bəyāḏî* 'YHWH will deliver you into my hand' (`be-yedkhem-nittanu`). *peḡer maḥănēh pəlištîm* 'the corpses of the camp of the Pelishtim'; *ləʿôp̄ haššāmayim* 'to the birds of the skies'. *kî yēš ʾĕlōhîm ləyiśrāʾēl* 'that there is Elohim in Yisra'el', literally 'that Yisra'el has Elohim': an anarthrous predicate (clause 2 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`), as 2 Kgs 1:3 'no Elohim in Yisra'el' (ASV 'that there is a God in Israel').

paragraphs.text: וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־הַקָּהָ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־לֹ֛א בְּחֶ֥רֶב וּבַחֲנִ֖ית יְהוֹשִׁ֣יעַ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנָתַ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: and that all this assembly may know that YHWH does not save with sword and spear; for the battle is YHWH's, and he will give you into our hand."

notes.official: *kî laYHWH hammilḥāmâ* 'for the battle is YHWH's'; *haqqāhāl hazzeh* 'this assembly'.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־קָ֣ם הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיִּקְרַ֖ב לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֑ד וַיְמַהֵ֣ר דָּוִ֔ד וַיָּ֥רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את הַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the Pelishtite arose and came and drew near to meet David, that David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Pelishtite.

notes.official: The second half of the verse (David running toward the battle line) is absent from LXX Vaticanus (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`; see v 12).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־יָד֜וֹ אֶל־הַכֶּ֗לִי וַיִּקַּ֨ח מִשָּׁ֥ם אֶ֙בֶן֙ וַיְקַלַּ֔ע וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י אֶל־מִצְח֑וֹ וַתִּטְבַּ֤ע הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ בְּמִצְח֔וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־פָּנָ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And David put his hand into the bag and took from it a stone, and slung it, and struck the Pelishtite on his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.

notes.official: *wattiṭbaʿ hāʾeḇen bəmiṣḥô* 'and the stone sank into his forehead'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּחֱזַ֨ק דָּוִ֤ד מִן־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי֙ בַּקֶּ֣לַע וּבָאֶ֔בֶן וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וְחֶ֖רֶב אֵ֥ין בְּיַד־דָּוִֽד׃

i18n.en: So David prevailed over the Pelishtite with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Pelishtite and killed him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.

notes.official: Absent from LXX Vaticanus. The verse anticipates v 51, where David kills Golyat with Golyat's own sword (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`; see v 12).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣רָץ דָּ֠וִד וַיַּעֲמֹ֨ד אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֜י וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־חַ֠רְבּוֹ וַֽיִּשְׁלְפָ֤הּ מִתַּעְרָהּ֙ וַיְמֹ֣תְתֵ֔הוּ וַיִּכְרָת־בָּ֖הּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּרְא֧וּ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים כִּֽי־מֵ֥ת גִּבּוֹרָ֖ם וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃

i18n.en: Then David ran and stood over the Pelishtite, and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath, and killed him, and cut off his head with it. And when the Pelishtim saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

notes.official: *gibbôrām* 'their champion', the word for a mighty warrior, different from *ʾîš-habbēnayim* in v 4.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וִיהוּדָ֜ה וַיָּרִ֗עוּ וַֽיִּרְדְּפוּ֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים עַד־בּוֹאֲךָ֣ גַ֔יְא וְעַ֖ד שַׁעֲרֵ֣י עֶקְר֑וֹן וַֽיִּפְּל֞וּ חַֽלְלֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ שַׁעֲרַ֔יִם וְעַד־גַּ֖ת וְעַד־עֶקְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And the men of Yisra'el and of Yehudah arose and shouted, and pursued the Pelishtim until you come to Gai, and to the gates of Eqron. And the slain of the Pelishtim fell on the way to Sha'arayim, as far as Gat and as far as Eqron.

notes.official: *wayyārīʿû* 'and shouted' (the war cry). *ʿaḏ-bôʾăḵā gayʾ* 'until you come to Gai' (ASV): *gayʾ* 'valley' taken as a place name; the LXX reads 'Gath', matching the end of the verse (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). Sha'arayim = Shaaraim; Eqron = Ekron (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִדְּלֹ֖ק אַחֲרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיָּשֹׁ֖סּוּ אֶת־מַחֲנֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el returned from chasing after the Pelishtim, and they plundered their camp.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח דָּוִד֙ אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת־כֵּלָ֖יו שָׂ֥ם בְּאָהֳלֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And David took the head of the Pelishtite and brought it to Yerushalayim; but he put his armor in his tent.

notes.official: *wayḇiʾēhû yərûšālāim* 'and brought it to Yerushalayim' (Jerusalem): an anachronism, since the city is taken only in 2 Sam 5. *bəʾohŏlô* 'in his tent'.

paragraphs.text: וְכִרְא֨וֹת שָׁא֜וּל אֶת־דָּוִ֗ד יֹצֵא֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אָמַ֗ר אֶל־אַבְנֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א בֶּן־מִי־זֶ֥ה הַנַּ֖עַר אַבְנֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְנֵ֔ר חֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אִם־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

i18n.en: And when Sha'ul saw David going out to meet the Pelishtite, he said to Avner, the captain of the host, "Avner, whose son is this youth?" And Avner said, "As you yourself live, O king, I do not know."

notes.official: Verses 55-58, absent from LXX Vaticanus, have Sha'ul ask whose son David is, although David has served him (16:14-23) (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). Avner = Abner (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`); *śar haṣṣāḇāʾ* 'the captain of the host' (cf. Josh 5:14). *ḥê-nap̄šəḵā hammeleḵ* 'As you yourself live, O king' (ASV 'As thy soul liveth'): the oath by the addressee's life (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`; `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׁאַ֣ל אַתָּ֔ה בֶּן־מִי־זֶ֖ה הָעָֽלֶם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the king said, "You inquire whose son the young man is."

notes.official: *hāʿelem* 'the young man', a rare word (cf. 20:22).

paragraphs.text: וּכְשׁ֣וּב דָּוִ֗ד מֵֽהַכּוֹת֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְרֹ֥אשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And as David returned from striking the Pelishtite, Avner took him and brought him before Sha'ul, with the head of the Pelishtite in his hand.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ שָׁא֔וּל בֶּן־מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה הַנָּ֑עַר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד בֶּֽן־עַבְדְּךָ֥ יִשַׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית הַלַּחְמִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Sha'ul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" And David said, "The son of your servant Yishai the Beit-Lechemite."

notes.official: *yišay bêṯ hallaḥmî* 'Yishai the Beit-Lechemite' (Jesse the Bethlehemite; `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).
